newsitem.title: USA: Cincinnati Bell backs $2.39-$2.40 FY96 EPS.
newsitem.headline: Cincinnati Bell backs $2.39-$2.40 FY96 EPS.

text.p: Cincinnati Bell Inc president and chief executive officer John LaMacchia said the company "can't quibble" with analysts' 1996 earnings estimates of $2.39-$2.40 a share versus $1.72 excluding special charges in 1995. It will report its third quarter about Oct. 16.
"The average of most of the analysts was at $2.39-$2.40," he said in a telephone interview late Thursday. "We haven't taken issue with that... We can't quibble with that."
Asked about some analysts' 1996 estimates as high as $2.45, he said, "That's getting on the high side."

Cautioning that next year is more difficult to predict because of regulatory and competitive issues and a major contract under review, he said estimates of $2.70-$2.75 offer "a decent range" that would be in line with the company goal of 15 percent a year earnings growth.

Chief financial officer Brian Henry, in the same interview, said a few analysts estimate 1997 earnings at $3.00. "We think that's unlikely," he said. "We would need to have a lot of good things happen" to achieve that earnings level.
